It also intersects with Nadia's finding — if governance reforms are the only thing the board will authorize, those reforms would still need to go through the special committee of three independent directors under our bylaws. And for Thomas's motion to dismiss strategy, this constraint means that if the motion fails and we end up in settlement discussions, our negotiating room is already defined by the board chair's instruction.

commitments.detail: Confirm within 48 hours the exact date the claim was received and whether the 10-business-day notice deadline has been met or is at risk. If not yet sent, send notice to the carrier immediately.
Prepare and circulate the motion to dismiss on demand-futility grounds based on the independence of five of seven directors. No answer to be filed at this time.

Update the board-resolution checklist to reflect the special committee requirement of exactly three independent directors for any governance undertaking. If governance reforms are pursued, convene the special committee before authorizing any resolution.

Formally document the board chair's instruction — governance reforms only, no monetary payment, no admission of wrongdoing — in the litigation plan so all counsel are working from the same constraints.

No response containing any admission or settlement terms may be authorized without prior written consent from the D&O carrier. Coordinate with Thomas and Nadia to ensure the motion to dismiss does not trigger consent requirements, and flag any future settlement discussions for carrier consent.

If the motion to dismiss is denied, any settlement discussions must adhere to: (1) governance reforms only, (2) special committee of three independent directors, (3) prior written carrier consent, and (4) no monetary payment or admission of wrongdoing.
